articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' QB/TE/DEF/K Blueprint for Week 10
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the onesies — QB, TE, DEF and K — for Week 10.
articles.body:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be a WR column , an RB column and this combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

Not all players are listed in the markets.

1. Josh Allen (at NYJ) - 23.7 proj. points

2. Brock Purdy (at DAL) - 22 proj. points

Purdy remains near the top of the league as fantasy's QB4 (22.4 PPG) on the back of elite efficiency, posting +0.31 EPA per dropback (QB2). His secret fantasy sauce is adding 25 rushing yards and the occasional ground score when the offense feels stuck. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are horrific defensively, allowing opposing QBs to average 19.9 fantasy points per contest. San Francisco enters this road tilt as 3.5-point road favorites with a massive implied team total of 29.5 points (second). Purdy is an elite QB1.

3. Joe Burrow (vs. PIT) - 20.7 proj. points

Burrow enters Week 10 as fantasy's QB1 (26.6 PPG) while delivering +0.27 EPA per dropback (QB4). Over his last four starts, Burrow's output has exploded to 32.1 fantasy points per game and +0.43 EPA per dropback (QB1), tossing 16 passing touchdowns in that heated stretch. Cincinnati leads the NFL with a 66% neutral pass rate (first), and they face a Steelers defense whose opponents pass 60% of the time in neutral situations (first). Pittsburgh has been tough on signal callers overall, allowing the 29th-most half PPR points to QBs (14.3). Even so, Burrow hung 24.6 fantasy points and three touchdowns on them back in Week 3. The Bengals enter as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (fifth).

4. Drake Maye (at DET) - 20.6 proj. points

Maye has surged into the upper tier of fantasy passers, sitting as the QB3 (22.6 PPG) with +0.09 EPA per dropback (QB16). His rushing baseline has been a constant weapon, adding 24.2 rushing yards per game (10th) across nine starts. If we look at Maye's highs and lows, it's clear that there is a sensitivity to opponent strength. He's beaten up on soft opponents since Week 4, and he'll get another one here, potentially with A.J. Brown returning.

The Lions have allowed the most fantasy points per game (23.6) on the most passing yards (277 YPG). Suddenly-benched QBs Kyler Murray (QB10) and Jacoby Brissett (QB7) had some of their most productive games of the year against them. New England enters this indoor road spot as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 24.5 points (10th).

5. Trevor Lawrence (at TEN) - 19.3 proj. points

Lawrence enters Week 10 as fantasy's QB12 (19.6 PPG) while generating an efficient +0.30 EPA per dropback (QB3). He has thrown multiple passing scores in four of his past five starts.

His Week 10 matchup is as friendly as they come against a Titans defense allowing the fifth-most half PPR points per game to quarterbacks (20.4). They also just traded away their top two players on defense and allow the third-most points to QBs on the ground as a bonus. Jacksonville heads on the road as 10.5-point road favorites carrying a healthy implied team total of 28.5 points (third). This is another eruption spot.

6. Tyler Shough (vs. CAR) - 19.8 proj. points

Shough has at least 15.8 fantasy points in every game except for his date with the Vikings. He was essentially stood up there. Now that he has LT Kelvin Banks back and had the bye week to heal his own fractured left hand, it's time to take Shough seriously as a fantasy QB1. He's the QB8 on the season and could get more production out of his third receiver spot with Jordyn Tyson mixing in. Shough can run when needed, but he may not need to against the Panthers. We'll see if they can return EDGE1, CB1 or CB2 back here. The Saints have a 25.5-point team total (seventh).

7. Dak Prescott (vs. SF) - 17.9 proj. points

Prescott is coming off a 335-yard, two-touchdown performance against Indianapolis and currently checks in as the QB11 in half PPR scoring (19.7 PPG). He has been efficient through the air with +0.18 EPA per dropback (QB9) while generating 264.6 passing yards per game (sixth). He'll welcome back George Pickens in this contest, and the OL is back to full health again. It's one of the most friendly offenses in the NFL, and Prescott is still playing well.

The game environment is great, too. The game total is at a monster 55.5 points, with Dallas as dogs to the 49ers despite having a 26.0-point team total themselves. Kirk Cousins (QB11), Michael Penix (QB8) and Jayden Daniels (QB7) have created a three-game streak of a fantasy QB1 finish.

8. Jared Goff (vs. NE) - 18.2 proj. points

Goff struggled against the Packers and Vikings because of how strong those defenses are, then dudded against the Dolphins in Miami. That was out of character. Goff is now the QB15 in fantasy on QB8 EPA per dropback. The hope is, the worst is behind him.

Up next is a New England defense ranking 14th in half PPR points allowed to opposing QBs (18.7 per game). The Patriots just surrendered a massive 36.2-point explosion to Jordan Love in Week 9 after Caleb Williams posted 22.1 points against them in Week 7. Detroit heads in as 2.5-point German favorites sporting a healthy implied team total of 27 points (fourth).

9. Patrick Mahomes (at ATL) - 19.4 proj. points

The Josh Downs trade will provide him with an answer against man coverage at the underneath and intermediate level. He's just far more polished than anyone else on the Chiefs. Even with poor WR play, Mahomes is the QB14 on QB12 EPA per dropback. He bottomed out against the Seahawks in Week 7 but has otherwise been a low-end QB1 option. The matchup is a clean one, especially with S1 Jesse Bates traded by the Falcons. Joe Burrow gashed them for 278 yards and four scores last week. Kansas City has a 24.5-point team total in this domed vacation.

10. Jayden Daniels (at NYG) - 18.1 proj. points

Daniels is still the QB1 in rushing yards per game (42.0), but they aren't calling designed runs for him since his elbow injury and that average is notably lower than his rookie season (52.4). The Commanders are getting some up-and-down play on go balls from their WRs since Terry McLaurin's injury, but Daniels does enough to hold onto low-end fantasy QB1 value. He's at least cleared 15.0 fantasy points in his five healthy games this year and is the QB13, including that elbow game.

Daniels ran all over the Giants in Week 5 in his return from said injury, posting a season-high 30.3 fantasy points and 103 rushing yards with two scores on the ground. DROY candidate Arvell Reese will look to make sure that doesn't happen here, and I don't like the Commanders' odds of their WRs beating this CB room now. Washington enters this divisional rematch as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 19.5 points (22nd).

11. C.J. Stroud (at CLE) - 16.5 proj. points

I wrote about C.J. Stroud a ton here . He's playing like a top-10 QB and has massively improved against the blitz and pressure.

12. Bryce Young (at NO) - 18.8 proj. points

Young has operated as fantasy's QB9 (20.2 PPG) across eight starts, pairing 272 passing yards per game (fourth) with +0.05 EPA per dropback (QB18). Carolina has stayed committed to the air, operating with the league's third-highest neutral pass rate (60%). He bounced back from a rough two-game stretch (TB and GB) with 24.3 fantasy points and three passing scores against Denver last week. It was an encouraging outing despite not having LG Damien Lewis.

The Saints matchup is one to attack. They've allowed the fifth-most passing yards (256) and sixth-most rushing yards (134). That's tough to do. They can rush the passer but everything else has been a major work in progress, especially just tackling. Young hasn't had a top-16 fantasy game against them throughout his career yet, but the Panthers' No. 12 team total (23.0) suggests that'll change here.

13. Jordan Love (vs. MIN) - 17.4 proj. points

Love has faced the most blitzes in the NFL, and he's handled it very well. He's scored the most touchdowns and compiled the most yards against it, largely throwing downfield darts to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Back in Week 1 against these blitz-crazy Vikings, Love hung 23.5 fantasy points on 387 total yards. He has the aggressiveness and WR talent to make defenses pay when bringing 5+. I can't wait to see if DC Brian Flores continues with a 75% blitz rate or finally cools off.

Love is a riskier start because Minnesota is still only allowing 10.9 fantasy points to QBs this year (easily the least), but Love is the QB2 in passing yards per game (291) and they don't have the run game to really pivot away from what's worked. Green Bay projects for 22.75 points.

articles.title: The Rock's cousin, who is a current top WWE star, admits "nepotism is a great thing"
articles.summary: The Rock has etched his name as one of the biggest WWE superstars of all time.
articles.body: The Rock has etched his name as one of the biggest WWE superstars of all time. While there have been many other names from the Anoa'i family who paved the way, arguably, The Great One is at the top of all of them. This would naturally mean that any of his relatives would get an easy path to enter WWE. In fact, one of his cousins is a top star in WWE today. She is none other than Nia Jax, who made a cold statement about the prevailing debate over nepotism in the company.The Rock's cousin Nia Jax on nepotism favoring her in WWEIn a recent interview on the Battleground Podcast, Nia Jax spoke about her tenure in WWE and how it began. The Irresistible Force said that she initially kept quiet about her rich lineage to find out if she had the merit to become a WWE superstar. Nia said, “Yeah, I mean, I think it’s so, you know, when I first tried out, like, I tried not to let anybody know that I was related to, you know, The Rock and the big Samoan dynasty because I wanted to hopefully get through with my own merits."When asked about fans heckling her for getting opportunities because of The Rock and her family, Jax did not downplay it and said that nepotism was great. She acknowledged that she got an easy entry into the WWE system, but proved her worth in the tryouts and eventually went on to become a top star in the current WWE women's division.She said,"It’s like, well, nepotism is a great thing, you know what I mean? I’m not going to sit there and negate all the accomplishments my family has made in this business. Like, I get to be a part of it. It’s incredible. And I’m not, like, I got an opportunity to try out just like everybody else does, and I made it. So there’s no reason for me not to be proud of my family and not to be proud of what they’ve accomplished."Nia Jax has been a multi-time WWE Women's Champion, one of the few women to compete in a Men's Royal Rumble, and has achieved other major accolades. Despite the criticism, Jax continues to move forward and carve out her own path in the TKO-led company.Also read: Cody Rhodes opens up about his potential WWE heel turn, says his character would look different than fansGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vivaan Kapoor clinches trap silver, LA quota
articles.summary: Pune: There was a lot of history riding on Vivaan Kapoor when he was shooting for gold in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on
articles.body: Pune: There was a lot of history riding on Vivaan Kapoor when he was shooting for gold in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Thursday.The Jaipur shooter missed creating some, while still becoming part of history, as he clinched silver and an Olympic quota for the Los Angeles Games. Vivaan, 24, became only the fourth Indian to win a World Championships medal in trap and only second after Karni Singh to win a silver.Manavjit Singh Sandhu is the only Indian to have won gold in the event at the Worlds, while Zoravar Singh Sandhu's bronze is the other medal India has won in this category.It was also the first time when two Indians entered a trap final in the World Championships. Other than Vivaan, Udaivir Singh Jaijee also entered the 8-man final, finishing sixth.In the final, Vivaan was in excellent form as he shot 29 clay out of 30. He was tied at 29 with Kuwait's Abdulrahman Al-Faihan as the match progressed to the shoot-off. Vivaan looked good in the shoot-off, but the Kuwaiti shooter too didn't budge and beat the Indian by one shot taking the shoot-off 3-2. The final was a strong field as it had Paris Games gold medallist Nathan Hales and silver medallist Ying Qi of China. While Qi took bronze with 22 hits, Hales got eliminated at the fifth position with the score of 11.Udaivir finished sixth with 11 hits.Earlier, in the qualification round, Vivaan and Udaivir faced a 7-way tie as seven shooters were tied at the score of 120. They faced the shoot-off for four spots and both Indians cleared the hurdle to get into the top-.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Javier Rodríguez Piris: "Queremos el Mundial de pádel 2030 en España"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la FEP visita MARCA con las copas de campeones del mundo
articles.summary: El presidente de la FEP visita MARCA con las copas de campeones del mundo
articles.body: Apenas han pasado unos días desde que España levantase en Doha (Qatar) la Copa de campeón del mundo de pádel por partida doble. Las chicas lograron el décimo campeonato y los chicos, el quinto, ambos tumbando a la otra gran potencia de este deporte: Argentina. Los dos trofeos visitaron ayer la redacción de MARCA con Javier Rodríguez Piris, presidente de la Federación Española de Pádel, a la cabeza. Orgulloso de lo logrado y aún con el subidón del éxito, ha sido recibido por el director adjunto, Emilio Contreras, y por el equipo de MARCA Pádel, donde ha repasado los éxitos logrados recientemente y también su etapa como mandatario cuando está a punto de cumplir un año. Pregunta: ¿Cómo se siente un bicampeón del mundo? Respuesta: La verdad es que estamos muy contentos. Ha sido una semana muy emocionante. Después de preparar todo el Mundial durante las semanas anteriores y de vivir toda la competición, traernos los dos campeonatos, las dos Copas del Mundo, nos hace estar muy, muy contentos. Pregunta: ¿Qué supone para una federación lograr los dos títulos más grandes que se pueden conseguir a nivel de selecciones? Es un inicio de mandato impresionante. Respuesta: Sí, la verdad es que llevamos casi un año y hemos tenido los Europeos de Menores, en los que hemos sido campeones, y la verdad es que está siendo un buen periodo. Ahora, ser campeones del mundo tanto en categoría masculina como femenina es un activo muy importante para nosotros y para la Federación. Es un orgullo poder sacar pecho y decir que somos España y que somos los mejores. Pregunta: ¿Cómo ha vivido la semana en Doha? Respuesta: La verdad es que ha sido una semana maravillosa. Tengo un recuerdo genial porque hemos convivido con todo el equipo y con toda la expedición oficial. Llevábamos dos delegados, que eran el vicepresidente primero y el segundo, el de Económico y el de Competición, Pepe y Paco. También llevábamos a los 16 deportistas, a los seleccionadores, Juanjo y Carolina, y a dos técnicos. Además, teníamos un jefe y un técnico de la URI, Guti, que han hecho un trabajo extraordinario. Han sido dos piezas clave. Después estaba el equipo de comunicación, con Nacho como director de Comunicación, Laura, Edu y Guillermo. También llevábamos a los dos fisioterapeutas. El lunes me reuní con toda la expedición y les dije que éramos un equipo, que cada uno tenía su función y que todos sabíamos lo que teníamos que hacer. Al final, se trataba de engranar toda esa maquinaria para conseguir las dos Copas del Mundo. Pregunta: ¿Cómo vivió el día de las finales? Respuesta: En principio, todo el mundo veía la final femenina bastante fácil para España, pero el partido se nos complicó en el encuentro que estaban disputando Paula y Gemma. Aunque en ningún momento vimos que peligrase la eliminatoria, nos fuimos al tercer set y empezaron los nervios. Empiezas a pensar que la cosa se puede complicar, pero al final salió bien. Después llegó el tema tan polémico de la alineación de Juanjo. En el primer partido todo el mundo estaba muy nervioso. Mirábamos las redes sociales y todo el mundo opinaba de todo. Luego está lo de Goñi, que fue extraordinario, y él es un encanto, un fenómeno. Había estado muy nervioso, pero al final Juan hizo un torneo y una semana maravillosos. Hizo un partidazo y Juanjo también los dirigió muy bien. El resto del equipo estuvo ahí, animando a tope, igual que las chicas. Pregunta: Presidente, ¿qué pensó cuando vio la alineación masculina? Respuesta: Honestamente, te digo que no me sorprendió tanto. Cuando viajé, yo estuve en Kuwait y dos días después viajamos juntos toda la expedición. Estuve hablando con los jugadores y les escuchaba. Notaba y me transmitían que estaban muy unidos, que eran un equipo. Comentaban las cosas que querían hacer y se les veía muy enchufados. Se lo dije en la reunión: 'Tengo buenas sensaciones'. Me estaba transmitiendo algo positivo y eso a veces se palpa. Tienes unas sensaciones que van más allá de lo que puedan decir los jugadores. Durante el partido, evidentemente, el resultado era complicado, pero siempre quedaba esa esperanza. Viendo cómo se estaban comportando y cómo estaba Juan, que en ningún momento dejó de luchar, de animar a Aimar, a Juanjo y a sus compañeros, había un ambiente especial. Además, esto es pádel. Como todos sabemos, puedes ganar un set por 6-0 y perder los otros dos también por 6-0. Al final, yo siempre tuve esperanza. Pregunta: Antes de todo el revuelo que se generó en las redes sociales, entiendo que la Federación Española está muy satisfecha con el trabajo de Juanjo Gutiérrez. Respuesta: Sí, la verdad es que Juanjo ha sabido manejar muy bien al grupo. Desde el principio, cuando acabamos en Kuwait, ya se vio su forma de trabajar. Estuvimos en la academia de Rafa Nadal, que está en Manacor, y allí se llevaron a cabo dinámicas de grupo con los jugadores. La verdad es que muy bien. Maneja muy bien el grupo. Yo nunca había estado en una concentración de este tipo con jugadores de este nivel y Juanjo sabe gestionar muy bien a los deportistas. Ha hecho una apuesta muy arriesgada y muchas veces, en esta vida, los campeones y los ganadores tienen que hacer apuestas arriesgadas. Pregunta: ¿Cree que estamos ante la mejor generación del pádel español de toda su historia? Respuesta: Yo creo que tenemos una generación femenina impresionante y en categoría masculina también contamos con algunos de los mejores jugadores. Siempre que me entrevistan digo lo mismo: tenemos a los mejores. En España tenemos lo mejor de todo el pádel: los mejores jugadores, los mejores técnicos, las mejores federaciones, los mejores gestores de federaciones, árbitros y clubes. Somos un ejemplo. En el Mundial se acercaba mucha gente y nos pedía consejo sobre determinadas cuestiones. Nuestra expedición era muy grande y el equipo de comunicación trabajó muy bien. Pregunta: ¿Por qué España es una de las principales potencias mundiales del pádel? Respuesta: Creo que se ha trabajado muy bien la base y desde la Federación estamos apostando por ello. En España ha habido técnicos muy buenos y gente que ha trabajado y sigue trabajando muy bien en las federaciones territoriales. Este es un éxito de las federaciones. Lo digo porque, sin el trabajo que hacen en formación, en sus campeonatos y en sus pruebas, esto no sería posible. Llevan muchos años trabajando muy bien y creo que otros países que están empezando deberían fijarse en cómo lo tenemos organizado en España. El trabajo de las federaciones territoriales con sus campeonatos es fundamental. A los jugadores también se lo dije en aquella charla: más allá de vuestro talento y de vuestro esfuerzo, que evidentemente sois grandes jugadores, ha habido una federación y una persona que se ha encargado de organizar un torneo, de preparar un campeonato y de conseguir que os animéis a jugar. Todo eso ha contribuido a que hoy estéis donde estáis. Siempre hay que pensar un poco de dónde se viene. En este caso, detrás están las federaciones territoriales, los técnicos, los organizadores, los presidentes de las territoriales, los gerentes y los árbitros. Somos un ecosistema de pádel muy importante. Pregunta: ¿Están otros países siguiendo ese camino de trabajo que está marcando España, desde la base hasta el profesionalismo? Respuesta: Sí, se está trabajando muy bien. En el Europeo de Menores de Oporto, por ejemplo, la final júnior fue contra Francia. Nos hicieron un set y estaban jugando Coquito y Iago, que forman una pareja muy buena. Había chicos de mucho nivel. También podemos ver que Italia, en categoría femenina, siempre está ahí. Ya quedó tercera en el anterior Mundial. Además, tenemos a Iciar Montes, que ha sido seleccionadora nuestra y que ahora está en Gran Bretaña, donde hay escuelas y jugadores españoles que están trabajando muy bien. También está Willy Lahoz, con quien estuvimos en Emiratos Árabes. Hay mucha gente trabajando fuera y la marca España está teniendo una influencia muy importante. En Europa, países como Países Bajos, Suecia y Portugal están trabajando muy bien. Los portugueses, por ejemplo, quedaron terceros en categoría masculina. Jugamos contra ellos en semifinales y tienen un buen equipo. Están haciendo un gran trabajo. Sé que en Portugal están yendo equipos desde Extremadura para trabajar allí, con técnicos y escuelas de competición que están desarrollando una labor muy interesante. Pregunta: ¿España ha dejado de crecer y está llegando a un grado de madurez o, como presidente de la Federación Española, considera que todavía hay margen de crecimiento? Respuesta: Yo te diría que se está produciendo una profesionalización cada vez mayor. Se está dando un salto importante en los clubes. Por ejemplo, en los clubes que conozco veo que antes se montaba uno en cualquier nave, con cuatro pistas, y poco más. Ahora los clubes que se están construyendo son grandes instalaciones profesionales, con un buen gimnasio, un buen sistema de servicios, cafetería e incluso residencias para alojar deportistas. Se está dando un salto importante. Después, a nivel de menores, también se está trabajando muy bien. Los técnicos están creando escuelas de competición importantes y hay que seguir en esa línea porque, como estamos comentando, vienen muchos países y los estamos viendo por el retrovisor. Ese es nuestro objetivo: trabajar mucho el pádel de base y la formación. También vamos a hacer cambios en 2027 en el ámbito formativo, porque cualquier organización que quiera progresar y crecer tiene que contar con un buen sistema de formación. Pregunta: ¿Cuáles son los objetivos generales que se marcó cuando llegaste a la presidencia, hace poco menos de un año? Respuesta: Yo me encontré una federación totalmente desestructurada. No voy a entrar en ejemplos concretos, pero había una falta de organización y de comunicación tremenda. Prácticamente no había nadie. Yo llegué el 23 de diciembre. Había sido elegido por la Asamblea el día 18 y, cinco días hábiles después, entró en vigor la resolución de mi nombramiento. Tenía que subir una noticia anunciando que era el nuevo presidente y tuve que redactarla, pegarla, colocarla, hacer un PDF y llamar al informático para que la subiera. Imagínate cómo estaba aquello. Además, veníamos de un proceso electoral largo, en el que hubo problemas entre varias candidaturas, y estaba todo bastante dejado de la mano. Creo que el anterior presidente llegó a un momento en el que pensó que aquello se quedase como estaba. Así que había que hacer una reestructuración completa. Pregunta: ¿Cómo es la relación actual con la Federación Internacional de Pádel? Respuesta: La verdad es que tenemos una relación buena y muy cordial. Con el presidente, Luigi Carraro, tengo muy buena relación. Al principio, cuando llegamos, había una serie de cuestiones con las que no estábamos de acuerdo, especialmente en cómo se estaban organizando las competiciones de CUPRA FIP Tour y los problemas que se habían generado posteriormente con los torneos de Premier Padel. No había un orden ni una coordinación con la Federación Española. Fue una de las primeras cosas que hablamos. Vimos que había que coordinar y regular las competiciones entre ambas partes para evitar que nos pisáramos. No podía celebrarse un CUPRA FIP Tour Bronce al mismo tiempo que un campeonato en una comunidad autónoma cercana, o que coincidieran un campeonato de menores y un torneo de Premier Padel en Santander y otro en Extremadura. En el resto de cuestiones, muy bien. El día 12 de octubre celebramos la Asamblea en Madrid, en el COE, y fue genial. Tenemos muy buena relación con Alejandro Blanco, presidente del Comité Olímpico Español, y su apoyo es muy importante para que el pádel pueda ser olímpico algún día, que es lo que todos queremos. Pregunta. Los Juegos Olímpicos. Siendo realistas, Javier, ¿cuándo cree que podría llegar la entrada del pádel en el programa olímpico? Respuesta: Ahora hay una oportunidad importante. Como comentaba, el presidente del Comité Olímpico Español, Alejandro Blanco, se presenta como candidato a la presidencia de ANOC. Las elecciones serán los días 6 y 7 de diciembre y sería un paso muy importante. Ojalá pudiera llegar para 2032, aunque quizá sea pronto. Si no, creo que para 2036 podría ser olímpico. El pádel cumple con creces muchos de los requisitos que se exigen: está presente en muchos países, hay muchísima gente que lo practica y existe un desarrollo importante. Se están haciendo muchas cosas y hemos participado en los Juegos del Mediterráneo. Estamos avanzando en hitos importantes dentro de todo el movimiento olímpico. Ojalá sea en 2032 y, si no, en 2036. Creo que es posible, la verdad. Pregunta: ¿Qué cosas tiene ahora mismo entre ceja y ceja para cambiar o modificar? Respuesta: Por ejemplo, me gustaría trabajar más en el crecimiento de las licencias federativas. Hemos acabado 2025 con 117.500 licencias. Se calcula que practican pádel unos cuatro millones de personas en España. Esta misma mañana estábamos ya cerca de las 120.000 licencias y las hemos superado. No sé si hemos llegado a un pico que no vamos a poder superar, pero creo que deberíamos trabajar más para que la gente se federe, compita con un seguro y esté respaldada por una estructura que permita tener un control. Hay muchas ligas que se organizan y que no están respaldadas por nada. Necesitamos saber exactamente cuánta gente juega al pádel y cómo se juega. Todo debería estar bajo el paraguas de las federaciones, porque cuanto más estructurado, regulado y controlado esté el deporte, mejor. Para mí es algo muy importante porque creo que podemos crecer mucho. Tenemos por delante al fútbol y al baloncesto, pero después ya estamos por encima del resto de deportes en número de licencias. Pregunta: ¿Cómo se puede acerca al practicante habitual de pádel que no consume pádel profesional a, precisamente, que lo consuma? Respuesta: Dándole visibilidad. Es lo que estamos intentando hacer hoy y lo que intentamos hacer siempre: traer campeonatos y pruebas a España. Yo siempre lo digo: me gustaría que en España hubiera un torneo Major y, por qué no, que en 2030 pudiéramos organizar un Mundial. Sería impresionante. Creo que España está muy preparada. En nuestro país se organizan pruebas de Fórmula 1 y de muchos otros deportes a unos niveles extraordinarios. Por eso, creo que la forma de acercar el pádel a la gente es conseguir que lo vea y que lo sienta más cerca. Hay que darle mucha visibilidad. Ya planteé esta cuestión en la última presentación del P1 de Madrid. Lo comenté y también lo he hablado con el presidente de la Federación Internacional. Si en algún momento el Major se trasladase a otro sitio, podría abrirse la posibilidad de organizar un Mundial aquí, porque hay muchos países interesados en acoger pruebas. Estuve con el presidente de Japón y también quieren organizar una competición en China. En todos los sitios quieren llevarse pruebas. El pádel está creciendo muchísimo en Asia y cualquier día podríamos encontrarnos con el anuncio de un torneo de Premier Padel en China, Japón o algún otro país. Pregunta: ¿Ve factible entonces que España pueda organizar un Mundial? Respuesta: Estamos preparadísimos. Creo que tendría una difusión enorme y que España está preparada. Este país está preparado para organizar cualquier tipo de evento de esas características si se planifica con tiempo. Sería increíble, impresionante. Intentaremos trabajarlo ahora que tenemos tiempo. El Mundial de 2028 ya está previsto que se celebre en Qatar, así que tenemos margen para trabajar, hablar y ver si alguna institución se presta a organizarlo. P. Habría dos mundiales en 2030 en España. R. Sería impresionante. articles.title: Harry Kane breaks caps record as England reach Nations League knockouts
articles.summary: England moved to second spot in Group A3 behind Spain, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.
articles.body:
Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England cap with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarterfinals.

Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid another embarrassment after their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kickoff at Wembley.

But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in Group A3 behind Spain, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.

Thomas Tuchel’s men have a chance to avenge their 3-2 defeat against the world champions in their Nations League opener when they travel to Madrid for Sunday’s clash.

Spain beat Czechia 2-0 in Prague on Thursday.

“After the first game when we lost here against them [Spain], we knew we left a bit out there,” Kane told ITV.

“We knew we could’ve done a bit better. We said to ourselves, ‘Let’s win every game until the next one and see what happens’. It’s the perfect opportunity now on Sunday to try and prove ourselves.”

England and Croatia struggled to get out of second gear in the opening stages of their match in London.

Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute, and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.

Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion, following a neat move by the home side.

Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball the first time across the area towards Rogers.

Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.

England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time.

The home side were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period.

But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner.

The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home.

Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area.

Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty, but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot.

Kane made no mistake, drilling home for a record-extending 92nd England goal.

Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive.

James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back, but Bellingham was in an offside position when he received the ball.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off, taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

A giant banner was raised before kickoff with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

articles.title: Ukraine war: Finland, Norway block visas for Russian athletes
articles.summary: Finland and Norway have announced fresh restrictions on Russian athletes, making it difficult for them to compete in the two Nordic countries as the war
articles.body: Finland and Norway have announced fresh restrictions on Russian athletes, making it difficult for them to compete in the two Nordic countries as the war in Ukraine continues.Finland announced on Thursday that it would restrict visas for Russian athletes, saying they had "no business" in the country as long as the war continued. Hours later, Norway said it would stop professional Russian and Belarusian sportspersons from competing on its soil.The decisions could affect major international sporting events scheduled in both countries.Finland says Russian athletes have 'no business' in countryFinland has tightened rules for Russian citizens applying for short-term work visas, including those seeking to take part in professional sports.Under the new rules, "Russian citizens will only be allowed to work under a Schengen visa in tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests," the Finnish foreign ministry said in a statement.The restrictions will also apply to Russian athletes competing under a neutral flag. They will not be allowed to obtain visas to enter Finland."As long as Russia's war of aggression continues, Russian athletes have no business in Finland," Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said in a statement."Their entry into the country would be a threat to Finland's international relations."The new rules will come into effect on November 16. Finland shares a 1,340-kilometre (830-mile) border with Russia.The country is scheduled to host the Figure Skating World Championships in Tampere in March 2027. The International Skating Union (ISU) said it was "studying" the possible impact of Finland's decision."The aim of the change is to prevent entries that Russia could use to spread messages supporting its war," Valtonen told reporters.Russia uses "sports as a tool for propaganda", she added.Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga welcomed Finland's move. In a post on X, he urged other European countries to "close the remaining loopholes, and strengthen coordinated pressure on Russia,".Norway also blocks Russian and Belarusian athletesNorway announced its decision a few hours after Finland. Its government said the country already had strict visa rules for Russian and Belarusian citizens.However, recent "relaxations introduced by international sports federations" could allow more athletes and support staff from the two countries to travel to Norway for competitions.The new decision could prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes from competing even if they have been cleared by the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS).Norway is preparing to host the Cross-Country Skiing World Cup in Trondheim in December.ISU questions Finland's decisionThe ISU said it believed athletes should not be held responsible for the actions of their governments. It said "that athletes should not be punished for the actions of the governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing".The governing body added that it was seeking "further clarifications" from the Finnish organisers.CAS ruling brings Russian ice hockey team back into focusFinland's decision comes after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on October 30 opened the possibility of the Russian ice hockey team returning to the World Championships next year. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), which has banned Russia from competitions since its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, had opposed the CAS decision.Several countries, including Finland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic, have said they would refuse to play against Russia at the World Championships in Germany.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also said last week that Russia would not be allowed to compete at the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championships in Alberta. The Finnish city of Turku has announced that it will withdraw from hosting the 2027-28 edition of the tournament if Russia takes part.Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin last week praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for "taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles". He also criticised countries that are opposing Russia's return to international sport.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia captain Pat Cummins denies involvement in ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal
articles.summary: Cummins says Khawaja was ‘100 percent wrong’ in claiming the whole team knew about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
articles.body:
Australia captain Pat Cummins ⁠has again denied any involvement in ⁠the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in a Test against South Africa in 2018, describing the allegations in Usman Khawaja’s autobiography as “utter nonsense”.

Former Australia batsman Khawaja, whose autobiography was published on Tuesday, said last weekend that all the players in the team knew about ⁠the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing. His latest comments triggered calls for a new investigation into the incident.

The scandal centred around the third Test in Cape Town, but Khawaja also claimed the tactic was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth.

“When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he’s 100 percent wrong. I’ve said that consistently for the last eight years,” Cummins told a news conference in Sydney on Friday.

“I did not know that was happening, but I think ⁠Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that.

“He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That’s complete and utter nonsense.

“There was no master plan around using illegal methods,” he added. “There’s no grand plan. There’s no team meeting. There’s no bowlers saying ‘this is what must happen’.”

Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan.

Darren Lehmann, who was the Australian head coach at the time, has also denied any knowledge, as has former batting coach Graeme Hick, who called Khawaja’s allegations “absolutely false”.

Cummins spoke for 68 minutes on Friday, taking every question from the media and saying he would never discuss the ball-tampering incident again.

The Australia skipper also took exception to Pakistan-born Khawaja’s contention in the book that the colour of his ‌skin and background had prevented him from becoming Australia captain.

“I think of all the things that I’ve read this week, I think that’s actually the most serious,” he said.

“Him saying that if you’re Australian captain, you have to be a certain skin colour, I couldn’t disagree with that statement any more.”

Steve Smith and David Warner, the then-Australia captain and vice-captain, were banned by Cricket Australia from elite cricket for a year for their roles in the ball-tampering.

Opening batter Cameron Bancroft, who brought a piece of sandpaper onto the field, received a nine-month suspension for his part in the ball-tampering.

“I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam to be careful when using sandpaper. That’s not the Usman that I know,” Cummins said.

“It’s not the Usman that has helped rebuild the Australian cricket ⁠culture over the last eight years.”

Later on Friday, Warner said the trio had paid a heavy price for the incident and revealed ⁠that his wife Candice had lost a baby in the aftermath of what became known as “ Sandpapergate “.

“I still stick by Uzzie and what he has written in that book. It is the truth,” the former Test opener said in TV commentary ahead of a one-day international between Australia and England.

“I actually feel for [Khawaja] at the moment. I actually feel that the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus and I’m very disappointed ⁠by that.”

Cummins was asked about Khawaja’s recollection that two players had rejected the batsman’s call for the team to take collective responsibility for the ball-tampering.

“I don’t remember any conversation around collective responsibility,” he said.

“So then, I’ve got no idea who ⁠those two people would be because I don’t remember ever being asked or having a conversation about it.”

Khawaja and ⁠Warner have also been critical of the Cricket Australia investigation in 2018 that found the three punished players solely responsible for the plot.

“I got asked to be part of that review,” Cummins said. “I was totally truthful. I’ve been very consistent since then at that event till now. Nothing’s changed.”

Earlier this week, the head of Cricket Australia ruled out opening another investigation into the 2018 incident.

Cummins said he respected the right of Khawaja to tell ‌his story in the autobiography but felt some of the allegations were very serious and had to be addressed.

“Usman’s a friend, but friends aren’t casual with each other’s lives and reputations,” he said.

“In his book, Uzzie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket.”

Cummins added, though, that he would not ‌be ‌taking legal action against Khawaja over the allegations in the book.

“I did get advised this week that some of the things that’ve been said are probably defamatory, but I won’t be doing that,” Cummins said.

“You’ve got to move on. It’s been eight years. We’re moving on. So, you got to draw a line at some point.”

articles.summary: At just 11, Indian footballer Riaan Ghodawat has already experienced something that many young players can only dream of.
articles.body: At just 11, Indian footballer Riaan Ghodawat has already experienced something that many young players can only dream of. On October 26, 2026, he became the first Indian to attend the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, where he got a chance to be around some of the biggest names in world football.A member of the Real Madrid Academy India, Riaan has already had several opportunities to experience football at the international level. articles.title: Legendary coach Terry Waters finds new role at Fishburne
articles.summary: After 49 years of coaching, Hall of Famer Terry Waters is transitioning to athletic director at Fishburne.
articles.body:
WAYNESBORO — Terry Waters is a legendary wrestling coach in the area.

He was inducted into the Virginia Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2022, and his photo and biographical info are in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in Stillwater, Oklahoma. Most assumed he would coach wrestling until he retired and then just walk away.

Raised in a hot bed of wrestling in Pennsylvania, Waters was a student at Milton Hershey School, a boarding school for low-income families in Hershey. He and his brother were among the first Black students at the school after it integrated.

Locally, Waters has coached at Staunton, Riverheads and Fort Defiance high schools, as well as at Washington & Lee University, where he was an assistant. He came to Fishburne in 2015.

This past summer, he announced he was retiring from coaching. It seemed to be the end of an amazing career, but then he announced, not too longer afterward, that he would be staying at the Waynesboro school to serve as athletic director.

He's now through the fall season and about to start winter sports.

"It hasn't gone totally smooth, but it's been a great transition," Waters said. "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids."

He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging.

"You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually."

Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be.

"I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well."

Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued.

"When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open."

Every year, at least in recent years, someone would ask the veteran coach how much longer. His answer was always one more year. He'd talk with his wife about his future in coaching after the season ended. She would tell him if he still had the energy and the desire, he should keep coaching.

"My brother pretty much summed it up when he told me if you like what you're doing, there is no sense in retiring," he said.

But this summer, he clearly remembers waking up one morning and thinking, "I'm done." He told the Fishburne staff about his decision. He was planning to just walk away, but then the athletic director position opened. Waters decided to apply.

"I've had athletic directors across the state send me notes telling me if I needed any help just let them know," Waters said. He said Frank Kahrs at Grace Christian has been particularly helpful. He's also talked with Staunton's David Tibbs about some questions he had. All the connections Waters has built over the years are proving to be helpful in the new job.

"I believe I'm here because it's where God wants me," Waters said.

The day-to-day life of an athletics director is never the same, and never boring, Waters said.

"You spend a lot more time than I actually though on the computer," he said, "sending emails out, setting schedules, things like that."

It's about a 10-hour a day job, give or take, and Waters said he's fine with that. He does have two assistant athletic directors that help take some of the burden off of him, but Waters said he'll be at every home event at Fishburne. He feels it's his responsibility.

Wrestling this winter may be the toughest for him because he's not coaching — although, maybe not.

"I don't think I'm going to miss it as much as other people think I'm going to miss it," Waters said. "I just want to make sure I don't step on toes."

Rick Palmer is taking over as head wrestling coach at Fishburne. Waters said he has confidence in Palmer's abilities to continue leading the program. Still, Waters said home wrestling events will be difficult, sitting in the stands watching instead of in the corner of the mat coaching.

"That is something that will be hard," he said, "but I'm prepared for that. I've done all I want to do in coaching in 49 years. I don't have anything else to prove. I was ready to step down. I was comfortable in my decision."

articles.title: 6 takeaways from Commanders' TNF win over Giants
articles.summary: Six takeaways from the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders got a much-needed win on Thursday, defeating the New York Giants 24-21 to improve to 3-5-1.

It wasn't easy, as the two teams traded the lead throughout the game. It looked like the Giants were about to put it away late in the fourth quarter when Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels threw his second interception of the year — on back-to-back possessions. However, the defense kept getting stops when it mattered; Daniels found redemption with a game-winning touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs.

Washington's defense won it when cornerback Rasul Douglas picked off JJ McCarthy.

Here are six takeaways from a huge Commanders' win.

We know about Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs and Sonny Styles, but Washington was also helped by several others. Ben Sinnott had a career night, catching four passes for 46 yards and a touchdown and showing what he can do with more opportunities. Safety Jeremy Reaves has quietly had a really good year. Reaves was everywhere on Thursday, hitting JJ McCarthy and in coverage. He also recovered a fumble. Reaves also finished with nine tackles. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler didn't put up big numbers, but had some tough runs. Nick Allegretti returned to the starting lineup and played well. How about Luke McCaffrey's heads-up play on the kickoff return on the final possession? Huge play. A true team win for Washington.

Jayden Daniels has battled a lot of adversity the last two years. This year, there was the elbow injury, the late-game shenanigans against the Giants in Week 5 and coming up just short against the Rams and 49ers in recent weeks. But the one thing he hadn't done was throw an interception. On Thursday, he picked a bad time to throw his first — and his second — interception. They came on back-to-back possessions. But fortunately, the defense bailed him out. Daniels, like any great quarterback, has a short memory. He led the Commanders on a game-winning drive, beating the pressure to find Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown. There has been a lot of talk about whether Daniels takes enough chances. It's foolish talk. He takes chances; he's just excellent at protecting the ball. He slipped up on Thursday, and his teammates had his back. He had theirs, too. Daniels needed a win like that. So did his team.

Things looked bleak for a moment when JJ McCarthy found Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard touchdown to put the Giants back up 21-17. What made it frustrating was that defensive coordinator Daronte Jones called the perfect blitz on third-and-7. However, safety Nick Cross let up, allowing McCarthy to get a throw off. Had Cross simply kept going or put his hands up, that play would never have happened, and the Commanders would have gotten off the field. It would be interesting to hear from Cross about why he hesitated. He once again played a terrific game, but that's probably one he'd like to have back. Ultimately, it didn't cost him.

Washington came into the game as the worst team on third downs. Against a good New York defense, the Commanders converted on 7 of 14 third downs. It was a combination of Daniels throwing the ball, smart playcalling, clutch short-yardage runs and Daniels using his legs. Everything worked. Washington's third-down performance was one of the primary reasons it won on Thursday.

We still aren't sure what Daronte Jones' future is in Washington. But in the last few weeks, he certainly looks like a keeper. The defense is playing much better. He's aggressive, and players are getting better each week under his watch. We've witnessed far too many times over the years a Washington defensive coordinator play it safe late. They get burned almost every time. Jones wasn't having it. On three straight plays, he went after McCarthy. All three plays went in the Commanders' favor, with the final one being a Rasul Douglas game-winning interception. A terrific night for Jones and offensive coordinator David Blough. Even more impressive, it was on a short week.

The last time the Commanders and Giants played, New York came after Daniels every time he dropped back. While they didn't pressure as often on Thursday, they tried, and the Commanders' offensive line shut them down. Nick Allegretti was back in the lineup at center and played well. No snap issues. He also didn't allow a single pressure. The interior of the offensive line — outside of Sam Cosmi — has been criticized often this season. For good reason. On Thursday, they stepped up, cut down on the pre-snap penalties and looked much better than they did five weeks ago. Daniels was sacked only once and had a clean pocket for most of his attempts.

articles.title: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team
articles.summary: All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is made up of members of the area programs and includes Coach of the Year Ken Delaney of Coldwater.
articles.body:
BATTLE CREEK - Never losing a game from late August until October. Winning a conference title and a district crown.

For helping his team accomplish all of that, Coldwater's Ken Delaney is the 2026 All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team Coach of the Year.

The All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is selected by nominations from the city and area coaches and voted on by the Enquirer sports staff.

In his 18th season as head coach, Delaney is on a roll with state-ranked teams in back-to-back years as the Cardinals were 15-2-2 overall. Coldwater finished as Interstate 8 Conference champs with a 6-0 record in the league and won a second district title in the last three years. Along the way, Coldwater went unbeaten from August 20 until the regionals and climbed to as high as No. 12 in the Michigan Interscholastic High School Soccer Coaches rankings in Division 2.

Delaney is joined on the All-Enquirer team by Cardinals players Abdulhamid Munassar, Ahmen Norman, Riath Shamaala and Jensely Norvilus.

Lakeview finished as All-City Tournament champs and adds Mang Sung, Richard Lian and Cristian Duran to the team.

Harper Creek had the most wins in program history as Beavers' Jake Cushman, Broderick Hanger and TJ Ruble were named All-Enquirer.

Also from the city, earning All-Enquirer honors, are Pennfield's Philipp Kruetz and Everett Wilkins, Battle Creek Central's Yoani Bautista Trejo and Deangelo Crape, with the St. Philip/Calhoun co-op program adding Ashton Heighton and Ben Kaczanowski.

Among area teams, Marshall's Brandon Baker, Rowdy Joseph, Carson Clapper and Trenton Wolkiewicz were named as All-Enquirer members, as well as Gull Lake's Charlie Trantham, Ethan Waldorf.

articles.title: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep
articles.summary: Panthers follow up rout of Mustangs with a tough win over Cougars in front of big crowd.
articles.body:
Just two weeks into the season and the Bloomington South girls basketball team has vanquished it's two county rivals.

The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. So it was a great early-season introduction to a sectional-like atmosphere for both teams in front of a vocal crowd at South on Thursday, Nov. 12.

Offense was hard to come by as the Panthers held off a second-half rally by North, getting a huge 3-pointer from freshman Quinn Wurtzman with 2:10 left in a five-point game to pull out a 48-37 win. It followed a much less rowdy 62-20 rout of Edgewood on Tuesday.

"We knew it was going to be a great crowd," North coach Kiley Jarrett said. "That's what we wanted. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was.

"I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference."

Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more.

"Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way.

"And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring."

South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line.

"We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens."

Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far.

"They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something.

"If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up."

South (2-1) will always lean on its defense, and forcing 11 turnovers in the first half led to some easy buckets and a 29-16 lead at the break. North had some key players in early foul trouble and the physical affects of the South press led to some 'tired' errors.

"It was just mistakes on our part," Jarrett said. "Foul trouble didn't help us at all, it got us out of our typical rotation."

But the Panthers' offensive struggles peaked in the third, going 2-of-11, forcing up some tough shots in the lane all night. That allowed the Cougars (0-2), who had just five more turnovers and played strong half-court defense most of the night, to chip away at the deficit.

"We know that when we play them that if we can keep them in the half-court and not turn the ball over, then we're going to be in good shape," Jarrett said.

North got within 33-27 at the end of three, but South wouldn't let them get any closer. A jump hook by Quinnly Fife and a banked in 3 by Avery Schwartzman from the top of the key while being fouled made it 38-29 with 6:26 to go.

But a 3 from Rilynn Williams, who had a game high 13 points, made it 40-35 with 2:40 left.

"She definitely is a more assertive player this year," Jarrett said. "And she stepped up tonight and made some huge plays for us. That 3 from the corner was absolutely huge. And I thought she did a good job defensively on Lehr."

But that's when Wurtzman took the next big shot of the night, knocking home a 3 from 22 feet to start an 8-0 run that put the game away.

"Knowing Quinn, she was ready for that shot and she'll be ready for that again," Jarrett said "It may say she's a freshman but she doesn't play like it and we knew that coming in.

"Credit to her. That was a momentum changer because I definitely felt like momentum was on our side before that."

All the same, Winters is looking at the big picture with his younger players.

"That was a big 3 but there were three layups she missed," Winters said. "If you're going to make the long one, make the short one. But that's the pressure of playing in your first North-South game."

South started the week with a 62-20 win at Edgewood, a game that got away quickly after the young Mustangs tied it at 8-8 with 1:40 left in the first quarter.

The Panthers scored the next 22 points as Edgewood coughed it up 20 times in the first half. It was 31-10 at the break and South put the running clock in motion late in the third, up 49-13.

Edgewood was limited to four field goals, just one inside the arc. The frustration was evident, but South is also likely the best team the Mustangs will see all season.

"You just have to harp on the positive things that we did," Edgewood coach Noah Stuckey said. "I feel like, that first quarter, we competed as well as we possibly could. We handled their physicality and got to the free throw line and then we just kinds of wore down.

"We got punched and wilted a little bit and didn't bring the energy in the second half."

It was just the second varsity team for the entire lineup so the speed and strength it takes to succeed at that level was on display.

On either side of that loss against the best team on their schedule, the Mustangs opened with a win over Greencastle 42-32 and then topped South Putnam 40-31 on Thursday.

"It felt awkward," Stuckey said of the win over Greencastle. "We started very strong, we got in some foul trouble and they made a run at us. Then, the second half, Kaitlyn (Ripley) took over. She didn't play the second quarter and had 23 points.

"The way they've been playing maybe the last couple of years is just stand and watch her," Stuckey said. "And we just can't rely on her to do everything. We've got to help her out and we kind of got in that run in the second and third quarter (against South)."

articles.title: Bears Stadium Bids Flood In As Developers Push City Plan
articles.summary: Developers pitch a $10 billion stadium plan for Chicago while the Bears eye Indiana. The city fights back with bold new offers.
articles.body:
Developers are flooding the market with unsolicited bids to keep the Chicago Bears in the city, but the team's focus remains on a suburban deal or a move to Indiana. This bid arrives as the Bears prepare for a legislative session in Illinois starting Nov. 17, yet the franchise has not endorsed any of these urban proposals.

The group plans to span about 100 acres and include a stadium for 75,000 fans alongside thousands of new homes. They argue that an urban site offers better economic value than remote suburbs. "It is our belief that a modern, competitive dome stadium such as the one that we are proposing will outperform suburban locations such as Arlington Heights or northwest Indiana," said Quintin Primo III, founder and executive chairman of Capri Investment Group, during a news conference in Bronzeville, according to Yahoo . Local leaders back the idea, but the NFL has previously flagged the specific Reese parcel as too narrow with active rail lines running through it.

While local boosters push for a downtown solution, the Bears are actively exploring a path across the state line. Nearly nine months ago, Indiana state leaders approved a funding package, and due diligence has been completed regarding two potential locations in Hammond. The team has not commented on the specific Chicago proposals but is watching the Illinois political process closely. "We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks," the Bears said last week regarding the two states, according to Yahoo Sports . The franchise is seeking property tax certainty and infrastructure help, with its main focus still on its own land in suburban Arlington Heights.

Capri's group is prepared to purchase the Bears' current Arlington Heights property, which would solve the land issue but force the team to abandon its preferred suburban setup. Chicago 4th Ward Alderman Lamont Robinson voiced strong support for the Bronzeville plan, stating it serves the community best. "I believe with everything I have, it's the right thing for the 4th ward. And the right thing for Chicago and the bears," Robinson said. The developers claim their plan will shape the city for generations, but the team holds the real power in the negotiation.

Newly reelected Gov. JB Pritzker intends to advance a Bears-related bill during the upcoming veto session, creating a critical moment for the stadium saga. The recent rise in developer activity suggests growing confidence that a bill could pass, even as the team keeps its Indiana option alive. The Reese option joins similar unsolicited offers made in recent weeks for sites at the former South Works steel mill and Rate Field. "We have an opportunity to make a decision that will shape Chicago for generations," said Quintin Primo III, Capri founder and executive chairman. The Bears must decide soon if they will stay in the city or leave for a new home.

Due diligence was completed on two potential locations in Hammond after Indiana state leaders approved a funding package nearly nine months ago.

articles.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI to provide welcome distraction to sandpaper scandal
articles.summary: England experienced more misery in Perth having thrown away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago
articles.body:
England crashed to a heavy defeat in the first game of their latest Australian tour, with a rousing debut from 21-year-old Mahli Beardman diverting some of the home side's attention from the ongoing sandpaper scandal .

Australian cricket is in the midst of a bitter civil war over Usman Khawaja's historic ball-tampering allegations but the hosts still eased to a seven-wicket victory in in the first ODI in Perth , where local boy Beardman collected stunning figures of six for 24.

It proved another calamitous visit to Optus Stadium for England, who thew away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago.

With Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood all rested between Test series, Australia pieced together an inexperienced attack and watched as it dismantled their rivals. At one stage England were 65 for eight and staring at a record low total, with some late repair work by the tail lifting them to 131 all out.

Travis Head missed the chance to repeat his match-winning Ashes knock when he was bowled cheaply by Gus Atkinson but skipper Mitch Marsh took up the mantle, clubbing 50 off just 30 balls to lead a chase that was all over in less than 24 overs.

England were criticised last winter for being too casual in their preparations Down Under but that has not been the case this time. They have trained hard, given themselves time to acclimatise and beaten Western Australia in a warm-up game at the WACA.

All of that work came to nothing, though, as they followed up a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan with a fourth loss in their last five outings.

After being sent in England's openers scraped together 24 before Australia bagged their first, Ben Duckett slashing Spencer Johnson to backward point.

Tom Banton came closer than anyone to finding form, hitting five fours on his way to 25 before driving with hard hands at the tidy Xavier Bartlett.

An average start then transformed into a dreadful once as the introduction of Beardman plunged the innings into turmoil.

Kicking off his senior international career with England's two best batters at the crease, the youngster got the best of both. His eighth ball was sharp and well directed, with enough swing to take the outside edge as Harry Brook went back in defence.

Joe Root , on the day he became just the third Englishman to 200 ODI appearances, was even bigger scalp. Muddling his way to 17 from 36 balls, he was put down by Cooper Connolly on three before an optimistic drive off Beardman wound up in Josh Inglis' gloves.

The celebrations showed how much that wicket meant but he was just warming up. Jordan Cox followed to another defensive nick and Beardman showed his range by bouncing out Sam Curran , who hooked obligingly to fine leg for a seven-ball duck. Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut.

England's woes continued as Jamie Overton 's ugly top-edge was plucked one-handed by the returning Johnson but Will Jacks ' 25 and Atkinson's punchy 29 not out saw them double their total.

Beardman returned to end the innings, dismissing Jofra Archer to claim record debut figures for Australia and match England's best ever analysis in the format, by Reece Topley in 2022.

Atkinson bowled Head with his first delivery but Australia never threatened to let the result slip. Marsh put his foot down, blazing four sixes and four fours, effectively settling the matter by the time flicked Overton to deep-midwicket in the ninth over.

Banton misjudged a steepling catch to spare Connolly on five, who added 22 more before poking Archer to gully.

Inglis and Matt Renshaw did the rest with minimal fuss, leaving 159 deliveries unused.

articles.title: Yorkshire re-sign paceman Ali on T20 deal
articles.summary: Yorkshire re-sign Pakistan fast bowler Hassan Ali on a two-year T20 Blast contract for 2027 and 2028.
articles.body:
Pakistan fast bowler Hassan Ali has signed a new two-year T20 Blast contract with Yorkshire for 2027 and 2028.

The former Warwickshire paceman has committed himself to a sixth successive summer playing in the Blast following his initial arrival in English cricket at Edgbaston in 2023.

Ali claimed 27 wickets at an average of just 13 in his first campaign with Yorkshire, helping head coach Anthony McGrath's Tykes reach the quarter-final.

"My time at the club this year was brilliant," he said. "Whilst it was disappointing in how our T20 season finished, there's a lot to build on."

"Hassan's impact this year went beyond the pitch," said Yorkshire general manager of cricket Gavin Hamilton.

"Anthony and I have consistently said we want to build long term relationships with overseas players to provide that continuity that we value so highly. Hassan signing for a further two years is an illustration of that."

The fixtures are yet to be released for next year's Blast, but it is expected to start in May, with the final again at Edgbaston on Saturday 17 July.

articles.title: Ireland bounce back to beat UAE in Emerging Nations
articles.summary: Ireland Women recover from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in th...
articles.body:
Ireland Women 171-5 (20 overs): Lewis 71, Maritz 29; Thirukkumaran 2-20

United Arab Emirates Women 110-8 (20 overs): Oza 51, Dharnidharka 18; Murray 2-21

Ireland Women recovered from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in their second game in Ajman.

The UAE won the toss and elected to field first, with Lloyd Tennant's side producing a much stronger showing with the bat than they did against Sri Lanka.

The opening partnership of vice-captain Amy Hunter and captain Gaby Lewis laid the foundations for the Irish.

Hunter managed 29 runs from 27 balls before she was run out by Suraksha Kotte, while Lewis finished as Ireland's top run scorer with 71, including 12 fours and a six before she was dismissed by Indhuja Nandakumar in the 12th over.

Janani Thirukkumaran then forced out Louise Little (seven) in the next over and claimed her second wicket from Lara Maritz soon after, although she did add 29 to Ireland's tally from just 23 balls.

Laura Delany was 18 not out while Theertha Satish ran out Alana Dazell (11) as Ireland finished on 171-5 from their 20 overs.

The UAE had a nightmare start to their response as they lost Satish, Heena Hotchandhani and Rinitha Rajith all inside the first two overs.

Samaira Dharnidharka added 18 to the tally before becoming the fourth player to exit when she was bowled out by Cara Murray in the seventh over.

Esha Oza steadied the ship as she registered 51 runs from 45 balls with five fours and a six before being dismissed by Little.

The wickets continued to tumble as Thirukkumaran (13), Mehul Kulkarni (six) and Athige Sashikala Silva (four) all went as UAE fell well short of the target, ending with 110-8.

Ireland will next be in action on Monday when they face face Papua New Guinea (09:15 GMT) before rounding off their group campaign with a game against Scotland on Wednesday, 18 November (05:00 GMT).

articles.title: SEC Football Week 11 Predictions: Picks for Every Game
articles.summary: It's a dangerous week with Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and Kentucky all trying to avoid a third loss. Here are our previews and predictions for every SEC game...
articles.body:
There's no hard and fast rule that the College Football Playoff can't pick an at-large 9-3 team over a 10-2 team from a Power Four conference, but it's never happened before. You're on your own if you want to risk it. However, several SEC teams will be in CFP mix even with a third loss, but the freakout will come if Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and/or Kentucky get that third hit. Even worse, it's over if any of the three-loss teams – South Carolina, LSU, Ole Miss, or Missouri – lose. Here are our quick previews and predictions for every SEC game. – Predictions: ACC | Big Ten

Texas at LSU is the highest-profile SEC game of the week, but Missouri at Georgia could become a 2026 season-changer if the Tigers come up with something big.

It's a dangerous week for Alabama and Tennessee, going on the road to deal with desperate Mississippi State and Vanderbilt teams, respectively.

The pressure will mostly be on Kentucky. It dropped big in the CFP after loss to Tennessee, and it can't afford a loss to Florida.

Game Time: 12:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN2 Location: Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, MS The best thing to happen to Mississippi State during a five-game losing streak is the announced signing and return of star quarterback Kamario Taylor for next year. The Bulldog defense has been great, but the offense isn't moving well enough to push past a decent D. Auburn might be working too hard, but the defensive front is great at getting into the backfield and should come up with just enough big stops late to hold off a late Bulldog rally in a terrific game. Prediction: Auburn 27, Mississippi State 24 Consensus Line: Auburn -2.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 3

Game Time: 12:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: FirstBank Stadium, Nashville, TN No. 3 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, Alabama has love from the committee, and now it just has to finish the drill with Chattanooga and Auburn to close. First, it has to take down a Vanderbilt team that finally came up with its first SEC win of the season, beating Mississippi State 25-23. Alabama might not be its sharpest out of the gate – a hangover effect from the 31-13 win at LSU – but just when it seems like this might be interesting, the Commodore turnovers will come. Bama will convert off all three turnovers it generates. Prediction: Alabama 37, Vanderbilt 17 Consensus Line: Alabama -18.5, o/u: 50.5 ATS Confidence: 3 | Must See: 2.5

Game Time: 3:00 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kyle Field, College Station, TX Over the last few years, SEC fans have liked to use the word gauntlet when it comes to some teams' tough schedules. In Tennessee's case, the term applies, facing Alabama (CFP No. 3), South Carolina (CFP No. 17), and Kentucky (CFP No. 11) in the last three games, and with LSU up next after what qualifies as a week off at Texas A&M. The Aggies have been brutally close to finally pulling off something meaningful, but it's 1-5 in the SEC after a heartbreaking loss at South Carolina. The defense that can't generate a sack will have a hard time on third downs, but it'll be a tough effort at home that comes just short against a Volunteer defense that continues to take the ball away in bunches. Prediction: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 20 Consensus Line: Tennessee -2.5, o/u: 44.5 ATS Confidence: 2 | Must See: 3.5

Game Time: 3:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: Georgia -14.5, o/u: 47

Game Time: 4:15 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Memorial Stadium, Norman, OK There's nothing like seeing Georgia run out of the tunnel in your ballpark and watching it conduct a light scrimmage. Ole Miss didn't have any answers in a 42-7 loss to the CFP No. 1 team last week, and now it has to go on a roll to have any prayer of being considered for a high ranking by the playoff committee. Oklahoma continues its schizophrenic season, following every win with a loss. The defense was brilliant in a 23-7 win over Florida, but it won't have the same luck against an Ole Miss offense that needs to stop turning the ball over. Star Rebel running back Kewan Lacy is out for the season, but Trinidad Chambliss will bounce back from his rough day against the Bulldogs with a sharp day. Too many decent Oklahoma drives will end up with field goals. Prediction: Ole Miss 23, Oklahoma 19 Consensus Line: Oklahoma -1.5, o/u: 49.5 ATS Confidence: 2.5 | Must See: 3.5

Game Time: 6:15 PM ET | TV: ESPN Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY CFP No. 11 Kentucky is still 7-2, with a playoff spot almost certainly for the taking if it can beat Missouri and Louisville. It has to get past the ugly 34-6 loss to Tennessee last week and keep its Florida groove going. The Wildcats have won four of the last five in the series. Before that, the Gators went 32-1 going back to 1986. It's all about the ground game with the Gators. They're 5-0 when running for over 120 yards, and 0-4 when running for that many or fewer. Kentucky got rumbled over by Tennessee, South Carolina, and Alabama. It's about to get hit by a good day from the Gators as they rebound big after last week. Prediction: Florida 28, Kentucky 24 Consensus Line: Kentucky -3.5, o/u: 52.5 ATS Confidence: 1.5 | Must See: 4

Game Time: 7:30 PM ET | TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA Prediction: Full CFN Game Preview and Prediction Consensus Line: LSU -4.5, o/u: 46.5

Game Time: 7:45 PM ET | TV: SEC Network Location: Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, AR Don't get totally caught up in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Soon, there will be big arguments about several three-loss teams and how worthy they might be. South Carolina started 2-3, but it's rolling with a four-game winning streak. That's not why the CFP No. 17 team has reason to dream of finishing in the top 12. Next week? Georgia. Beat the No. 1 team, drop Clemson, and all of a sudden, there will be a discussion. First, it has to get by a plucky Arkansas team that's far better than the 3-6 record might indicate. Nothing comes easy for the Gamecocks. Star quarterback LaNorris Sellers is banged up, but he's expected to go. Fortunately for 16, Arkansas doesn't have a pass rush to get to him.
